text:
Jamie Drysdale didn't dress it up afterward. "It was ugly. We didn't play very well, but we found a way," he said, as posted by Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports. That's about right. The Philadelphia Flyers trailed the Ottawa Senators 5-2 early in the third period and won 6-5 in overtime.

For most of the night Ottawa was the better team. The Senators owned the second period, 1.45 expected goals to 0.28 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and Dylan Cozens and Drake Batherson turned a 1-1 game into 3-1. Philip Tomasino opened the third with his 100th career point, and Cozens scored again at 5:27. By the full count of shots, Ottawa deserved to win 70% of the time.

Then the floor gave way under Samuel Ersson, facing the Flyers team that drafted him and later dealt him away. Cam York, who had already scored late in the second, snapped in a power-play goal at 6:25, and Tyson Foerster scored at 6:40 on a 5% chance. With Joseph Woll pulled for an extra skater during four on four, Drysdale tied it at 17:27. Ersson allowed 4.15 goals more than his 19 shots deserved, a brutal number on a night his team out-attempted Philadelphia 61 to 38.

Travis Konecny ended it 39 seconds into overtime, a shot that O'Connor wrote "just barely trickles through Sam Ersson," for the Flyers' first overtime win of the season. Konecny finished with a goal and three assists and added the most wins of anyone in the game. It came days after RMNB and others reported the Flyers could ask him about waiving his no-movement clause, and Drysdale singled him out: "TK, a heck of a game, took charge, especially in that third period."

Rick Tocchet's team has now beaten Ottawa twice in three meetings this season. Ottawa's three-game winning streak is over, and the Senators let go of a game they controlled for most of the night.
headline: Flyers erase a three-goal hole, Konecny wins it
